page.layout: One printed page. Running head at the top, with the page number beside it. One column of running text, with a Greek and Latin marginal note at the left, level with the lines "&adiunctorum loci" and "enim tum beneficium". The catchword "&c" stands at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: ne iudicamus: quia honestum: quia laudabile: quia cum virtute coniunctum: & ad eandem merita atq; beneficia accepta traducenda sunt omnia: vt illa quoq; ornari solent, quæ nobis vel summè necessaria: vel commoda plurima maximáque adferunt: vel iucunditatem atque voluptatem aliquam pariunt: aut prædicantur ab iis, in quos collata: quæ ad effectus referuntur. Amplificantia etiam hîc adhibenda, quæ comparatorum potissimùm, ἀὐξητικὰ am plificantia.& adiunctorū loci suppeditant. Magnum enim tum beneficium videtur, cùm comparatur cum aliis: aut ostéditur: amicum, vel primum, vel solum, vel inter non paucos præcipuum extitisse, qui beneficium contulerit. Circumstantiæ itidem rei, personæ, modi, temporis, loci, sua natura exigua beneficia commendant, augent, amplificát: atq; efficiunt, vt grata sint ea: quæ data vltrò, non precibus atq; intercessione impetrata: quæ data non temerè, sed consilio certo: quæ data cum aliquo periculo, aut offensione aliorum: quæ data à viro magno, summaque authoritate prædito: quæ data indignis, neq; eiuscemodi aliqua promeritis: quæ data citò, tempestiuè, sæpe: quæ deniq; diuturna, stabilia, &c

page.notes: The Greek marginal word is hard to read at this scan size; it is taken as ἀὐξητικὰ (augmentative) and marked as doubtful. The reading "potissimùm" is taken from the printed form "potifsimùm". The final "&c" is treated as a catchword, since it stands alone below the last line at the right.
